gaps.discriminates: Placental abruption vs. other causes of antepartum hemorrhage (e.g., placenta previa, vasa previa) — abruption is the only one that commonly causes consumptive coagulopathy with falling fibrinogen; normal fibrinogen would reduce likelihood of moderate-severe abruption.

gaps.info: Targeted placental ultrasound findings (e.g., retroplacental clot, hypoechoic area)
gaps.discriminates: Placental abruption vs. placenta previa or marginal sinus varix — ultrasound can directly visualize retroplacental hematoma (specific for abruption) or low-lying placenta (previa), though sensitivity is limited.

gaps.info: Uterine tenderness and uterine activity (e.g., tetanic contractions, board-like rigidity)
gaps.discriminates: Placental abruption vs. preterm labor or uterine hyperstimulation — uterine tenderness and hypertonus are highly characteristic of abruption and not explained by labor alone.
